axis: plainly suitable → propriety pushed past its purpose

members.tone: The plain baseline of the family - approves a thing as suitable, right or appropriate without naming the standard it is measured by.
Warm approval - what accords with custom is credited with grace rather than mere compliance, unlike the dry *decorous*.
Gentle and pleased - it finds conduct agreeable in its accord with propriety rather than measuring it against a rule.
A phrase rather than a word, and formal to the point of ceremony - approval delivered by invoking the code instead of describing the conduct.
Cool and external - conduct is held up against a standard of propriety and passes, with none of the warmth of *becoming*.
Understated - grants that conduct accords with propriety without the ceremony *decorous* brings to the same verdict.
Approval as a verdict - the social rule was met, and nothing warmer than that is claimed.
The bluntest way to render the same social judgement as *correct*, carrying no formality at all.
Approval keyed to the occasion and the people in it rather than to any code - it praises harmony where *correct* praises compliance.
Modest and human - it grants that a thing suits the persons and the moment, with less deliberation than *fitting*.
A designation rather than a compliment - it states that something is proper or legitimate under a named law, and the approval belongs to that law and not to the speaker.
Informal and reassuring - declares a thing proper or legitimate, above board and open to no objection.
Contemptuous - the excess of propriety is read as self-satisfaction, correctness worn as superiority over others.
The lightest fault in this group - propriety held so tightly it stiffens, mocked rather than condemned.
Dismissive and faintly ridiculing - the overdone propriety is treated as fussiness, silly rather than severe like *priggish*.
Propriety inflated into squeamishness - more disapproving than *prim*, since the excess is taken as a readiness to be shocked.
